History_of_Present_Illness.content: Stool consistency varies during the day, sometimes watery and sometimes loose.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Stool: varies during day (watery at times vs loose)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Drinking plenty of fluids by mouth.

Medications.content: Patient reports using a medication called "Lexapro" and states it is an inhaler that is yellow.

Family_History.content: Father died of bowel cancer about 10 years ago at age 62.
Family_History.source_text: died of bowel ca ~10 yrs ago at age 62

Assessment.content: Acute diarrhea for 3 days with 4–5 bowel movements per day, mild abdominal pain, one episode of emesis, no blood or mucus in stool, possible low-grade fever, and tolerating fluids.
Assessment.source_text: 1. Acute diarrhea x3 days (4–5/day) w mild abd pain, emesis x1; no blood/mucus; possible low-grade fever; tolerating fluids.

Plan_of_Care.content: Encourage oral fluid intake for diarrhea.
Recommend soft diet including crackers, toast, and jam, and avoidance of dairy, fish, meat, and eggs during diarrhea.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Soft diet: crackers/toast/jam; avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs during diarrhea

Plan_of_Care.content: May use yogurt as a source of probiotics.
Consider over-the-counter Dioralyte for electrolyte replacement.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Consider OTC Dioralyte for electrolyte replacement

Plan_of_Care.content: If diarrhea persists for more than one week, consider stool sample.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
• Return/seek care if:
  • diarrhea persists >1 week (consider stool sample)

Plan_of_Care.content: Seek care if blood appears in the stool.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
• Return/seek care if:
  • ...
  • blood in stool

Plan_of_Care.content: Seek care if diarrhea frequency increases to around 6–8 times per day or there is concern for dehydration, as hospitalization may be needed.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
• Return/seek care if:
  • ...
  • ↑ frequency to ~6–8/day or concern for dehydration (may need hospital)

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient should return or seek care if diarrhea persists more than one week, if there is blood in the stool, or if frequency increases to about 6–8 times per day or there is concern for dehydration.
Follow_up_Information.source_text:
• Return/seek care if:
  • diarrhea persists >1 week (consider stool sample)
  • blood in stool
  • ↑ frequency to ~6–8/day or concern for dehydration (may need hospital)

Physical_Findings.content: Clinician notes patient is not dehydrated.
